I called Max tonight.
I understand, hormones are acting up. I simply wanted stewed meat!

Lyova, the most delicious duck of your life is on you!
Does anyone know where the nearest jewelry store is around here?
Next to the flower shop, across the street.
It looks like the chef is going to propose to Elena!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'guys, lads, kids (plural only)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Да нет, ребят, тут всё понятно.

examples.text: Ребята, вы где?
examples.trans: Guys, where are you?

examples.text: Ребята с тобой поработают.
examples.trans: The boys will have a word with you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да нет, ребят, тут всё понятно.

examples.text: А вы чего тут стоите?
examples.trans: And why are you standing around here?

examples.text: Я тут.
examples.trans: I'm here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Всё хорошо, девочки.
examples.trans: Everything is fine, girls.

examples.text: Вечно вы всё портите!
examples.trans: You always ruin everything!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нятно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Да нет, ребят, тут всё понятно.
examples.trans: No, guys, everything is clear here.

examples.text: Всё понятно.
examples.trans: All clear.

examples.text: Понятно, спасибо.
examples.trans: I see, thanks.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да, конечно!
examples.trans: Yes, of course!

examples.text: Звони в любое время! Ладно, я пойду.
examples.trans: Call at any time! Alright, I will go.

examples.text: Звони в любое время!
examples.trans: Call at any time!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сегодня он ей подарок сделает, завтра она его в бар отпустит.
examples.trans: Today he will give her a gift, tomorrow she will let him go to the bar.

examples.text: Егор, слушай, Виктория Сергеевна попросила отнести это вино в номер, который она сняла.
examples.trans: Yegor, listen, Viktoriya Sergeyevna asked me to take this wine to the room she booked.

examples.text: Ну, скажите мне, почему вместо кулона появилось кольцо?
examples.trans: Well, tell me, why did a ring appear instead of a pendant?

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'арок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'gift, present' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Сегодня он ей подарок сделает, завтра она его в бар отпустит.
examples.trans: Today he will give her a gift, tomorrow she will let him go to the bar.

examples.text: Мы ваш подарок потеряли и купили кольцо.
examples.trans: We lost your gift and bought a ring.

examples.text: Это тебе подарок.
examples.trans: This is a present for you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Ты забыла? У вас послезавтра развод!
examples.trans: Did you forget? Your divorce is the day after tomorrow!

examples.text: Сегодня он ей подарок сделает, завтра она его в бар отпустит.
examples.trans: Today he will give her a gift, tomorrow she will let him go to the bar.

examples.text: Всё, что мне от тебя нужно, — это завтрашний развод!
examples.trans: All that I need from you is tomorrow's divorce!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'bar' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Сегодня он ей подарок сделает, завтра она его в бар отпустит.
examples.trans: Today he will give her a gift, tomorrow she will let him go to the bar.

examples.text: Наш бар закрывается.
examples.trans: Our bar is closing.

examples.text: Проверьте все бары и старых друзей.
examples.trans: Check all the bars and old friends.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'пустить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will let go', paired with 'отпускать'.

examples.text: Сегодня он ей подарок сделает, завтра она его в бар отпустит.
examples.trans: Today he will give her a gift, tomorrow she will let him go to the bar.

examples.text: Отпусти меня!
examples.trans: Let me go!

examples.text: Отпустить немедленно!
examples.trans: Release him immediately!

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'we shall see', paired with 'смотреть'.

examples.text: Можно я посмотрю?
examples.trans: May I have a look?

examples.text: Я только посмотрел.
examples.trans: I only had a look.

examples.text: А можно я пойду посмотрю?
examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'in the evening', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Какие планы на вечер?
examples.trans: What are the plans for the evening?

examples.text: А ты не можешь потерпеть до вечера!
examples.trans: And you cannot be patient until evening!

examples.text: Вот увидим вечером!
examples.trans: Well we will see tonight!
